summary: Tauri 2 app with two symmetric backends behind one frontend. Desktop mode: src-tauri/src/lib.rs registers 30 #[tauri::command]s (settings, accounts, discussions, terminals, kombai, pool, agent-room) and terminal.rs streams PTY output to the webview via app.emit("pty-data"/"pty-exit"). Web/SaaS mode: src-tauri/src/bin/cst-server.rs runs server.rs::run_from_env(), an axum server that mirrors nearly every Tauri command as an HTTP route under /api/* plus a WebSocket at /ws/terminals/:id; the frontend picks the mode at startup via client_startup_config (remote_mode + base_url + admin token, token auto-read from %APPDATA%/codex-switch-terminal-server/server.local.env.ps1). Auth for web mode is a single CST_ADMIN_TOKEN bearer header (query param ?token= for WS), checked per-handler; /healthz is the only unauthenticated route. Terminal transport is raw PTY bytes both ways: desktop = pty-data events + write_terminal/resize_terminal/stop_terminal commands; web = ServerWsMessage {type: data|exit|error|status|pong} JSON frames and ClientWsMessage {input|resize|stop|ping}. A broadcast channel (2048 events) buffers PTY output produced before/between WS connections so the initial Codex ANSI screen replays on connect. settings.rs owns the schema (AppSettings: accounts[AccountProfile{id,label,codexHome,projectDir,proxyId,startupCommand,limits,bypass}], proxies, agents[AgentProfile cli|ide], pool PoolConfig, kombai, agent_room, codex_bypass, auto_discover_accounts), persisted as pretty JSON at CST_DATA_DIR/settings.json or %APPDATA%/codex-switch-terminal/settings.json. It directly manipulates per-account Codex config: writes auth.json (chatgpt auth_mode + tokens) into ~/.codex-pool-<alias> or CST_DATA_DIR/codex-homes/pool-<alias> on import; upserts approval_policy="never" and sandbox_mode="danger-full-access" into config.toml via a hand-rolled TOML top-level-key lexer (ensure_codex_bypass_config, atomic tmp+rename); reads rate limits by spawning `codex app-server --stdio` JSON-RPC per account. The agent_room module (MCP server on 127.0.0.1:8123/mcp) already provides a message-bus with operator chat commands (room_send/room_messages with since-cursor) — the closest existing chat-shaped primitive. Discussions module parses Codex session JSONL for history dashboards (list_discussions, list_prompt_history), useful for chat transcript rendering.
keyFacts: The frontend talks to Codex ONLY through a raw PTY (xterm-style byte stream). There is no structured Codex event stream today; a chat UI must either parse ANSI/JSONL output, drive `codex app-server --stdio` JSON-RPC (pattern already exists in settings.rs read_server_rate_limits), or use `codex exec`-style protocols.

Desktop terminal events: app.emit("pty-data", {id, data}) and app.emit("pty-exit", {id}) from terminal.rs; frontend writes via invoke write_terminal(id, data), resize_terminal(id, cols, rows), stop_terminal(id).

Web mode mirrors desktop 1:1: cst-server (bin) serves the built frontend dist as static fallback, exposes /api/* JSON routes matching each Tauri command, and /ws/terminals/:id WebSocket with JSON frames ServerWsMessage{type:data|exit|error|status|pong} / ClientWsMessage{type:input|resize|stop|ping}. Mode selection happens in client_startup_config (CST_CLIENT_REMOTE / --remote / exe name contains 'cloud'; base_url from CST_CLIENT_BASE_URL or --remote-url=, default http://127.0.0.1:8080).

Auth (web): single shared CST_ADMIN_TOKEN, checked per-handler via Authorization: Bearer header (check_admin_header); WS accepts ?token= query param. Only GET /healthz is unauthenticated. CORS is very_permissive. Errors are JSON {error:{message,code}} with secrets redacted.

Web terminal buffering: broadcast::channel(2048) per session; the initial receiver is parked in pending_events so output emitted before the first WS connect (Codex's first ANSI screen) is replayed; on WS close the receiver is parked again for reconnect replay. Only ONE parked receiver — a second simultaneous viewer subscribes fresh and misses backlog.

30 Tauri commands registered in lib.rs invoke_handler: load_settings, client_startup_config, save_settings, ensure_account_home, import_account_docs, import_account_json, remove_account, account_limit_status, pick_project_dir, usage_dashboard, account_token_usage, list_discussions, list_prompt_history, claim_session_for_terminal, copy_discussion_to_account, delete_discussion, start_terminal, write_terminal, resize_terminal, stop_terminal, launch_ide, kombai_status, kombai_start, kombai_stop, kombai_install_extension, pool_start, pool_stop, pool_status, pool_pick_terminal_account, room_enable, room_disable, room_status, room_messages, room_send.

cst-server /api routes: /health, /admin/drain, /settings (GET+PUT), /accounts, /accounts/import, /accounts/home, /accounts/:id (DELETE), /limits, /usage, /account-usage, /discussions, /discussions/copy, /discussions/claim, /discussions/delete, /pool/status|start|stop, /terminals (POST start), /terminals/:id/write, /terminals/:id/resize, /terminals/:id (DELETE), /kombai/*, /workspaces, /workspaces/:id (DELETE), /fs/list, /room/status, /room/messages?since=, /room/send. Plus merged routers: pool::router (OpenAI-compatible proxy) and agent_room::router (/mcp).

Settings schema (AppSettings, camelCase JSON): accounts[{id,label,codexHome,projectDir?,proxyId?,startupCommand?,limits{connectedAt,sessionAnchorAt,weeklyAnchorAt},bypass=true}], proxies[{id,label,proxyUrl,note}], defaultAccountId, shell (powershell.exe default), codexCommand, autoRunCodex, proxyControlsEnabled, pool{port=8787,apiKey,defaultModel=gpt-5-codex,reasoningEffort,upstream=https://chatgpt.com,requestTimeoutSecs,cooldownSecs429,concurrency,clientIdOverride}, agents[{id,label,command,kind:cli|ide,builtin,loginCommand,statusCommand,doctorCommand}], activeAgentId, kombai{codeServerCommand,port=8899,extensionId,autoInstallExtension}, agentRoom{enabled=false,port=8123,secret}, codexBypass=true, autoDiscoverAccounts=false.
Settings location: CST_DATA_DIR/settings.json if set, else %APPDATA%/codex-switch-terminal/settings.json (XDG_CONFIG_HOME / ~/.config fallback). Agent room state persists in sibling agent-room/ dir.

auth.json manipulation: import_account_json/import_account_docs write a full Codex auth.json ({auth_mode:"chatgpt", tokens:{id_token,access_token,refresh_token,account_id}, last_refresh: RFC3339-micros}) into a per-account CODEX_HOME (~/.codex-pool-<alias> or CST_DATA_DIR/codex-homes/pool-<alias>). Accepts flat objects, accounts[].credentials exports, and ChatGPT web session blobs (accessToken reused as id_token when missing; ~10-day lifetime, no refresh). account_has_auth_tokens() checks tokens.access_token non-empty.

config.toml manipulation: ensure_codex_bypass_config(home) upserts top-level approval_policy="never" + sandbox_mode="danger-full-access" via a line-based TOML lexer (upsert_top_level_string / advance_toml_lex) that respects tables, multiline strings/arrays, comments; atomic write via config.toml.cst-tmp rename. Called per-terminal-start when account.bypass. agent_room also merges/removes an [mcp_servers.agent_room] entry in each CODEX_HOME config.toml on enable/disable.

Per-account isolation is done via the CODEX_HOME env var on each spawned PTY; each account has its own auth.json/config.toml/sessions dir. Proxy env vars (HTTP_PROXY etc.) injected per account when proxyControlsEnabled.

Rate-limit reads spawn `codex app-server --stdio` (JSON-RPC over stdio: initialize, initialized, account/rateLimits/read id=2, 18s timeout, stdin must stay open until reply on codex>=0.144) — this is a ready-made template for a chat UI driving Codex through app-server instead of a PTY.

Agent Room is an existing chat-like message bus: room_send(text, to?) posts as OPERATOR_IDENT, room_messages(since) returns {messages, cursor} for polling; same surface over HTTP (/api/room/*). RoomState is an axum MCP server on loopback; agents get per-terminal CST_ROOM_TOKEN.

Server terminal start (POST /api/terminals) accepts {accountId, repoUrl?|workspacePath?, branch?, cols, rows, command?, agentId?}; clones repos into ephemeral workspaces (7-day purge) or uses an existing dir confined to CST_WORKSPACES_ROOT; sends a banner line then optionally auto-types the startup command + \r into the PTY. Desktop start_terminal is the analogous local path (terminal.rs).

integrationPoints: Desktop PTY output: Tauri events "pty-data" {id, data} and "pty-exit" {id} emitted from terminal.rs — a chat UI would intercept these instead of feeding xterm.js

Desktop PTY input: invoke("write_terminal", {id, data}), invoke("resize_terminal"), invoke("stop_terminal"), invoke("start_terminal") — the chat input box would call write_terminal with the message + "\r"

Web PTY: WebSocket /ws/terminals/:id?token=<admin> — JSON frames {type:"data"|"exit"|"error"|"status"|"pong"} down, {type:"input"|"resize"|"stop"|"ping"} up; POST /api/terminals to start; parked broadcast receiver gives replay of pre-connect output
Mode switch: invoke("client_startup_config") → {remoteMode, baseUrl, token} decides Tauri-invoke vs HTTP/WS path; any chat UI must implement both transports to keep web parity

Structured Codex protocol alternative: `codex app-server --stdio` JSON-RPC (spawn pattern in settings.rs read_server_rate_limits with CODEX_HOME env) — the natural backend for OpenCode-style message/tool-call cards instead of ANSI parsing

Chat-shaped precedent already in codebase: room_send/room_messages Tauri commands and GET /api/room/messages?since=<cursor> + POST /api/room/send — cursor-polled message list the UI could reuse or copy
Transcript source: discussions.rs reads Codex session JSONL files under each CODEX_HOME/sessions — historical messages for rendering past conversations in the chat pane

Frontend containers: src/main.ts + src/platform.ts (modified in working tree) hold the xterm.js wiring and the desktop/web transport abstraction — the DOM-level place to swap terminal for a message list
Per-terminal env hooks: CODEX_HOME, CST_WORKSPACE_ID, CST_AGENT_ID, CST_ROOM_TOKEN injected into every PTY (both modes) — available to correlate a chat pane with its session

Startup command auto-typing: account.startupCommand (or request.command) is written to the PTY with trailing \r on start — same mechanism a chat UI could use to launch `codex` with specific flags (e.g. proto/exec modes)
risks: No structured event stream from Codex exists today: everything is raw ANSI bytes over PTY. Building message/tool-call cards requires either adopting `codex app-server`/`codex exec --json` (new plumbing in terminal.rs and server.rs) or fragile ANSI/TUI scraping.

Two transports must stay in parity: any new chat channel needs both a Tauri command/event implementation (lib.rs/terminal.rs) and an HTTP/WS mirror in server.rs, or web mode silently loses the feature.

Web WS replay supports only ONE parked receiver per session — a second concurrent chat/terminal view of the same session will miss buffered output; broadcast lag drops (RecvError::Lagged is skipped) can lose bytes under heavy output, tolerable for a terminal but corrupting for parsed structured streams.

Auth is a single shared admin bearer token with very_permissive CORS and per-handler (not middleware) enforcement — any new route added without auth_or/check_admin_header is unauthenticated by default (the /healthz handler relies on exactly this).

settings.json is rewritten wholesale by several commands (load_settings can self-mutate via ensure_agents/sync trackers); concurrent writes from desktop app + cst-server sharing the same CST_DATA_DIR could clobber each other — a chat UI adding new settings fields must round-trip the full AppSettings.

Codex accounts run with approval_policy=never + sandbox_mode=danger-full-access written into config.toml whenever account.bypass (default true) — a chat UI that surfaces 'approval' cards would conflict with this; approvals never reach the stream.
config.toml edits use a hand-rolled TOML lexer (not a parser); unusual TOML in user configs could still be mis-edited; the same file is concurrently touched by agent_room provision/deprovision.

Working tree already has uncommitted modifications (src/main.ts, src/platform.ts, src-tauri/src/lib.rs, server.rs, settings.rs, terminal.rs on branch feat/agent-room) — the mapped surface may shift when that branch lands, and this study read the modified (not committed) versions.
